data.summary: ddflow/services/prompts.py:342 render() builds jinja2.Environment(...) (not jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment, which services/export/registry.py:363 uses for exports). Templates come from <repo>/.ddflow/prompts/<name>.md and prompts/commands/ (prompts.py:12,285), i.e. from a committed repo or an org bundle. Probe (scratch, .venv python -I): P.render("{{ cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.getpid() }}") returned a pid, and "{{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()|length }}" returned 451. So cloning a repo whose prompt override carries that expression, then running a review, ddflow prompts get or MCP prompts/get, executes its code with the user's rights. Fix: SandboxedEnvironment (keep StrictUndefined) in render(), one shared factory for the other Environment sites (lanes/opencode.py:140, lanes/endpoint.py:153 render package templates only), and a test rendering the two probe expressions expecting SecurityError/TemplateError.
data.title: Prompt templates render in an unsandboxed Jinja environment: a .ddflow/prompts/*.md file runs code

data.summary: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py:25 SHAPES has no entry for these. Probe: R.Redactor('log', secret_patterns=session_secret_patterns(SessionConfig()), names=[], hostname='h', home='[REDACTED:path]').text(S).text == S (unchanged) for: glpat-<20 chars>, pypi-AgEI<60 chars>, SG.<22>.<43>, lin_api_<40>, dop_v1_<64 hex>, key-<32 hex> (mailgun), a three-part eyJ... JWT, 'AccountKey=<64 base64>==', and 'curl -u admin:hunter2hunter2 https://x'. Also 'mysql://root:Tr0ub4dor&[REDACTED:email]/db' becomes 'mysql://root:Tr0ub4dor&[REDACTED:email]/db': the email shape eats only the tail after '&', so the head of the password is committed to the log. EventLog._write (infra/log/_eventlog.py:271) relies on these shapes for every committed free-text field. Fix: add the provider shapes and a userinfo-in-URL shape (scheme://user:pass@host, whole password), with one test per shape in tests/ (a table, like the existing shape tests).
data.title: Log redaction shapes miss common credentials (gitlab, pypi, sendgrid, linear, digitalocean, mailgun, JWT, azure AccountKey, curl -u) and leak part of a URL password

data.summary: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_split/_commands/_head. Probe (check(cmd, Config(), env={}) returns None = allowed) for: '{ pkill x; }', 'if true; then pkill x; fi', 'for i in 1; do pkill x; done' (the keyword/brace becomes the command's first word, _head does not skip then/do/else/{/!), "bash -lc 'pkill x'" (only an exact '-c' word is looked into, forbidden.py:~150; '-lc', '-ec' are the common spellings), '`pkill x`', "eval 'pkill x'", 'pkill\<newline> x' and 'git\<newline> push' (lines are split on newline before shlex, forbidden.py _split, so a continuation is read as two commands), 'find . -exec pkill x {} \;', "echo 'pkill x' | sh". '$(pkill x)' IS caught. Agents write bash -lc and if/for loops routinely, so the guard added after three subagents ran pkill (module docstring) still misses ordinary forms. Fix: drop leading shell keywords and '{', expand combined short flags containing c for shells, join backslash-newline before splitting, look into backticks and eval strings, treat -exec/xargs/sh stdin as sub-commands; test table of the allowed list above expecting refusal.
data.title: forbidden_commands is bypassed by shell compound syntax: brace group, if/then/do keywords, bash -lc, backticks, eval, line continuation

data.summary: ddflow/services/forbidden.py matches an entry's flag words as written ('-rf' matches '-fr' only). Probe: check('rm -r -f .ddflow', Config(), env={}) -> None; check('find .ddflow -delete') -> None; check('mv .ddflow /tmp/x') -> None; 'rm -rf .ddflow' and 'rm -rf ./.ddflow/events' are refused. The event log is the source of truth, so the protected target should be the path (.ddflow with rm/mv/find -delete/unlink/shred/git clean), not one flag spelling. Fix: normalise separate short flags into one set before matching and add path-keyed entries; test table.
data.title: forbidden_commands entry 'rm -rf .ddflow' does not match 'rm -r -f .ddflow', 'find .ddflow -delete' or 'mv .ddflow x'

data.summary: ddflow/config/_coerce.py:46 _coerce returns any non-str raw unchanged ('if not isinstance(raw, str): return raw'), so only env strings are coerced. Probe (scratch repo, Config.load with .ddflow/config.toml): '[lease] ttl_s = true' -> ttl_s True; '[review] max_rounds = 2.7' -> 2.7 (an int knob holding a float, later range()/slice use raises TypeError); '[lease] ttl_s = -5' -> -5 (every lease already expired, any agent may take any claim); 'ttl_s = inf' and '1e400' -> inf (leases never expire); 'ttl_s = nan' -> nan; '[lease] heartbeat_s = 0' accepted. Counting config_sections via dataclass metadata: 530 knobs, 244 numeric, only 130 declare knob(check=...). Only ttl_s='abc' is refused (InvalidValue). Fix: _coerce_knob validates the declared type for TOML values too (bool is not int, no float for int, finite), and knob() takes minimum/maximum so a sweep adds ranges; ratchet: numeric knob without a check shrinks only. Org-locking cannot protect a value the loader never validates.
data.title: A TOML value of the wrong type or range reaches the Config unchecked: bool/float for int knobs, negative or infinite lease.ttl_s, 114 of 244 numeric knobs have no check

data.summary: ddflow/core/globs.py:114 overlap only treats * and ? as wildcards when taking the literal prefix; '[' is literal. Probe: overlap('src/[ab]x.py','src/ax*') and the reverse both return False although src/ax.py matches both (prefixes 'src/[ab]x.py' and 'src/ax' neither startswith the other; fnmatch of either pattern against the other fails). Two claims can therefore be granted on files they both write. Other class cases (src/[ab]*.py vs src/a*.py) are caught by luck of fnmatch. Fix: cut the prefix at the first of * ? [ and add a regression table with class cases.
data.title: globs.overlap misses a character-class glob against a literal-prefix glob (src/[ab]x.py vs src/ax*)

data.summary: ddflow/infra/log/_eventlog.py:296 opens <safe_filename(agent_id)>.jsonl; core/slug.safe_filename keeps any length (300 chars -> 300; 130 'é' -> 400 bytes), so ENAMETOOLONG (errno 36). Probe: 'ddflow --repo . --agent <300 x> session start' prints a Traceback ending in OSError File name too long from _stamp_and_guard -> _write; EventLog(Path('.'), 'x'*300).append(...) raises the same. --agent, DDFLOW_AGENT and the MCP as_agent are free strings (ddflow_identify documents max 64 but the per-call paths do not enforce it). Also 'a/b', 'a b', 'a:b' and 'a_b' all map to shard a_b.jsonl (distinct agents share a file; on a case-insensitive filesystem 'A' and 'a' collide in git). Fix: validate and cap the id once where it is resolved (refusal naming --agent), and make the shard name injective (digest suffix when sanitised or truncated).
data.title: An agent id longer than ~250 bytes crashes every append with an uncaught OSError traceback

data.summary: Measured 3 times: 'ddflow --version' 1.10, 1.12, 1.10 s wall, 77 MB RSS, on a loaded machine. python -X importtime: ddflow.surfaces.cli costs 907 ms cumulative of which ddflow.api is 866 ms (api.cirun 334 ms, api.gates 308 ms, api.lifecycle 292 ms); sys.modules holds 829 ddflow modules and 1301 in all after 'import ddflow.surfaces.cli'. Every hook call (PreToolUse, prompt hook, session start) pays this; hooks run per tool call. Fix: lazy command registry (import the api module of the chosen verb only; completion_fast.py shows the pattern), a hard fast path for --version/--help/hooks run, and a ratchet on 'python -X importtime' cumulative for the cli module.
data.title: ddflow --version takes 1.1 s: the CLI imports 829 ddflow modules before parsing a cheap command

data.claim: Structure rules are mostly ratcheted and clean (0 oversize files, dead code 0, 1 duplicate cluster, 1 subprocess home); the gaps are classes the ratchets do not see (inline literals, direct filesystem/shutil, refusal texts, numeric knob validation, redaction shapes, hook command parsing) plus 9 verified defects B7c5f77dd3e B3b5eb2055a Bc69e4cea5c B8844810c49 Bc2f54fd0db Bebc6fe14a1 Bc598dc2d6a Bb90f72f770.
data.falsifier: A re-run of the same scans after the AU- tasks showing no decrease, or any listed probe input now being refused/redacted/validated is the expected result; a probe still passing after its bug is closed falsifies the fix.
data.mechanism: AST scans of ddflow/ (7928 defs, 1047 files) plus probes of services.forbidden.check, core.redact, config.Config.load, core.globs.overlap, services.prompts.render, EventLog append, and python -X importtime.
data.probe: scratch scripts scan.py dup.py msgs.py and inline python -I probes (2026-11-03)
data.probe_output: files>27000B: 16, >30000B: 0; fully annotated defs 6559/7928 (82.7%); public docstrings 3106/4285 (72%); broad except 213 (61 swallowed); rw_text without encoding 170; direct time/sleep calls 241 (ratchet 216); print() in library code 358 (325 in surfaces); ddflow --version 1.10 s, 829 modules; refusal texts naming a CLI or MCP call: 56 of 409 api/ sites; structural duplicate clusters >=12 lines: 4
data.question: How well does ddflow conform to its own rules (configurable, managed, reuse, adapters, no-shell, tell-dont-discover, small-files) and what defects sit on its critical paths?
